captions.instagram:
What are density and buoyancy?

Why does a 100,000-tonne steel ship float while a nail sinks? Lower blocks of cork, ice, iron and gold into a brim-full can, load a cargo ship to its Plimsoll line, test Archimedes' crown, fly a hot-air balloon, dive a submarine and float in the Dead Sea.

→ Lower an iron block into water: the scale reads less, by the weight of the water pushed aside.
→ Ice is 0.92 g/cm³, so it floats with 92% hidden below the surface, like an iceberg.
→ A steel ship floats because its hollow hull pushes aside its own weight of water.
→ Archimedes’ crown test: silver makes a crown bigger, so water pushes its side up.
→ Air at 100 °C is 20% lighter than cool air: 2,800 m³ of it lifts a basket full of people.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/buoyancyclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: What are density and buoyancy? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Why does a 100,000-tonne steel ship float while a nail sinks? Lower blocks of cork, ice, iron and gold into a brim-full can, load a cargo ship to its Plimsoll line, test Archimedes' crown, fly a hot-air balloon, dive a submarine and float in the Dead Sea.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/buoyancyclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/buoyancyclear

In this video:
• Density and the upward push. Density is mass ÷ volume: water is 1 g/cm³, cork 0.24, iron 7.87, gold 19.3.
• Ships, clay and a crown. A steel ship floats because its hollow hull averages less than 1 g/cm³.
• Floating on air. Air at 100 °C is 20% lighter than at 20 °C, so a balloon of it lifts hundreds of kilograms.
• Swimmers, fish and submarines. A big breath makes most people float.
• Surprises and myths. Water is densest at 4 °C, so lakes freeze from the top down.
